Open Start and type your farm name, your country, the sales tax rate and your own limits in the yellow cells: weight difference you accept, late interest, claim days and the milk tiers.
List every buyer on Buyers with country, kind, payment terms and credit limit. Sales, rank, amount owed and credit left fill in by themselves.
Write each product on Marketing Plan with its expected tonnes, cost per tonne and the margin you want. Your minimum price and the market price fill in.
Type the weekly market price of each crop on Market Prices. The change and the 4 and 13 week averages fill in.
Record every delivery on Sales Lines with tonnes, price and deduction. Add the haulage on Haulage Costs and the truck weights on Weighbridge Tickets.
Enter orders on Sales Orders and forward contracts on Forward Contracts. Tonnes delivered come from the sales lines; then type what the harvest can still give on Contract Fulfilment.
Make one invoice for each delivery on Invoices and type every payment on Payments Received. Receivables Ageing shows who owes what and for how long.
Put the offers of buyers on Quote Comparison and read the best net price. Record claims on Quality Claims and export papers on Export Documents.
Use Market Day Sales, Livestock Sales and Milk Price Tiers for direct sales, animals and milk. Buyer Ratings scores each buyer; Bad Debts follows disputed money.

Use the 13 calculators for net price, best buyer, contract fill, price per kg, break-even, sell or store, invoice tax, late interest, minimum price, moisture, haulage, shortfall penalty and price trend.
Read Sales and Buyers Dashboard and Charts every week: sales, contracts, receivables, claims, haulage and market prices.

the same ledgers show which fields, crops and herds make money after their own costs, per hectare and per animal
expected sales, grants and costs, plus loan repayments and tax taken from their pages, give the closing cash and the weeks of costs it covers
every loan and credit line has its schedule, the principal repaid, the balance, the next payment date and a warning for a late repayment
applications, approvals, payments received and the amount still to come, with a warning before the evidence for a payment claim is due
sum insured, premium and renewal dates for each policy, and every claim with its days open and the amount still to receive
every payment due to the tax office, the council or a licensing body with days left and the amount still open, feeding the cash forecast
cost, life and scrap value give the yearly depreciation and the value of every machine and building, with the date of the next count
expiry dates for certificates, licences and permits, and each audit with its open actions and a warning when they are overdue
monthly chemical store, spray diary, animal movement and other records, with a check for those missing, late or due soon
margin, owner drawings share, debt service cover and current ratio for each quarter, set against the targets you choose

One row for each cost code with its yearly budget and the person who answers for it; spent so far, share used, the full-year forecast and a check fill in from the Cost Ledger.
Cost ledger: every cost by cost code, field and animal group
One row for each bill or payment with its cost code and the field, crop or animal group it belongs to; the cost group, payment status and the budget, profit and cash pages fill in from it.
Income ledger: every sale by source and buyer
One row for each sale or payment received with its source and the field, crop or animal group that earned it; the payment status and the profit pages fill in from it.
One row for each month; revenue, grants, costs, depreciation, profit, margin and the profit so far this year fill in from the ledgers, the grants and the asset register.
One row for each field with its crop and the person who answers for it; revenue, costs, profit, profit per hectare and margin of this financial year fill in from the two ledgers.
One row for each crop; the hectares in your fields, revenue, costs, profit, profit per hectare and margin of this financial year fill in from the fields and the ledgers.
One row for each herd or flock; revenue, feed and other costs, profit, profit per animal and margin of this financial year fill in from the two ledgers.
Cash flow forecast for the next 12 months
One row for each coming month: type the sales, grants and costs you expect; loan repayments and tax come from their pages, and the closing cash, the weeks of costs it covers and a check fill in.
One row for each bank account on each balance date; type the money in, the money out and the balance from the statement, and the net change fills in. The latest date is your balance now.
One row for each loan, mortgage or credit line with its lender, rate and term; the payment, the principal repaid, the balance, the next due date and a check fill in from the repayment schedule.
One row for each repayment due: the date, the payment and the interest in it; type the date you paid and the principal part, the status and the lender phone fill in.
One row for each application or payment with the officer who handles it; type what you applied for, what was approved and what you received, and the amount still to come and a check fill in.
One row for each policy with its insurer, the sum insured, the premium and the renewal date; the days left, the premium rate and a renewal check fill in.
One row for each claim with the policy, the event and the amounts; type the claimed and the settled amounts and the insurer, the days open, the amount still to come and a check fill in.
One row for each payment due to the tax office, the council or a licensing body; type the date you paid and the days left, the amount still open and a check fill in.
One row for each machine, building or work with its cost, life and scrap value; the yearly depreciation, the age, the value after depreciation and the date of the next count fill in.
One row for each certificate, licence or permit with the body that issues it; the days left and an expiry check fill in so that nothing lapses before an audit or a delivery.
One row for each audit or inspection with the inspector, the result and the actions left open; type the date the actions are due and a check fill in.
Compliance records for chemicals, sprays and animals
One row for each record that must be written each month; type the date it was completed and a check shows the records that are missing, late or due soon for the inspector.
Owner drawings and key ratios by quarter
One row for each quarter with revenue, costs, drawings and debt payments; profit, margin, drawings share, debt cover, current ratio and a check against your targets fill in.

Manager: monthly profit and loss ready
Hello, the profit and loss for the month starting {month} is ready. Revenue {revenue}, costs {costs}, profit {profit} and a margin of {margin}. Please read it before we meet.
Hello, the close of the month starting {month} is due. Costs show {costs} so far. Please enter all bills and payments and tell me when the figures are complete.
Hello {manager}, the cost code {name} has used {used} of its budget: {actual} of {budget}. The forecast for the year is {forecast}. Check: {state}. Please tell me the reason and what we can change.
Hello, our cash forecast for the month starting {month} shows {closing}, which covers {cover_weeks} weeks of costs. Check: {state}. Please look at sales dates and large payments.
Hello {owner}, {name} ({crop}, {area_ha} ha) shows a profit of {profit} this year, that is {per_ha} per hectare. Check: {state}. Please send me the reasons: yield, price or costs.
Hello, a payment on {scheme} from {body} has come in: {received} on {received_on}. Please record it in the bank log and tell the office.
Office: expenses to enter by Friday
Hello, please enter all expenses up to {date} in the Cost Ledger by Friday, for example {description} from {vendor} for {amount}.
Hello, the invoice from {vendor} for {amount} ({description}, {date}) is marked {state}. Please check it against the order and approve it for payment.
Hello, please match the {account} with the statement of {date}. We show money in of {money_in}, money out of {money_out} and a balance of {balance}. Tell me about any difference.
Hello, the payment {item} of {amount} is due on {due}. Status: {state}. Please prepare the payment and keep the receipt.
Hello, the licence payment {item} for {authority} is due on {due}. Please renew it on time and send me the receipt.
Hello, policy {pol_id} ({covers}) with {insurer} renews on {renewal}. The premium is {premium}. Please check the values and collect a second quote.
Hello, our repayment of {payment} on loan {loan} with {lender} is due on {due}. Please confirm the account details for the transfer.
Hello, we send our annual accounts for loan {loan_id} ({purpose}). The balance is {balance}. Please tell us if you need more papers for the review.
Bank: credit line increase for season
Hello, we ask for a higher limit on our {type}, {purpose}, for the coming season. The balance now is {balance} on {principal} borrowed. Please send the conditions.
Hello, please send a statement for loan {loan_id}. Our records show a balance of {balance} and the next payment on {next_due}. Tell us if you see a difference.
Hello, we update the list of security for loan {loan_id}: {collateral}. Please confirm that it matches your file.
Hello {officer}, please find our application documents for {scheme} attached. We apply for {applied}. Please confirm that you received everything.
Grant officer: evidence for a claim
Hello {officer}, we send the evidence for the payment claim on {scheme}. The evidence date is {evidence_due} and the amount still to come is {outstanding}. Please confirm receipt.
Hello {inspector}, we confirm your inspection on {date}: {scope}. Please tell us which maps, invoices and photos you want to see.
Hello, we report a {event} on {field} on {event_date} under policy {policy}. We claim {claimed}. Please send the claim form and arrange an assessor.
Hello, our policy {pol_id}, {covers}, renews on {renewal}. Please send a renewal quote for a sum insured of {sum_insured} and tell us what changed.
Insurer: photos and evidence for a claim
Hello, we send photos and evidence for claim {claim_id} ({event}, {field}). The status is {status} and it has been open for {days_open} days. Please tell us if you need more.
Inspector: audit date and records needed
Hello {inspector}, we confirm the {kind} on {date}. Scope: {scope}. Please tell us which records you need and we will have them ready.
Hello {inspector}, here is our reply on the {kind} of {date}: {actions_open} actions are open and due on {action_due}. Please confirm that the plan is accepted.
Hello, our certificate {name} expires on {expiry}. Please send the renewal steps, the fee and the audit dates.
Hello, we send the figures for the quarter starting {quarter}: revenue {revenue}, costs {costs} and profit {profit}. Please check them and tell us what the year-end needs.
Hello, we count the assets on {next_count}. Please check {name} ({class}), its condition and its place. The value after depreciation is {book}.
Hello {owner}, the record {type} for {period} was due on {due}: {state}. Please complete it today, because inspectors and buyers ask for it.
Profit and loss statement of a month
Profit and loss statement of {set:firm}, dated {today}.
Revenue from sales was {col:pnl.revenue} and grants received were {col:pnl.grants}. Costs were {col:pnl.costs} and depreciation was {col:pnl.depreciation}.

The profit for the month is {col:pnl.profit}, which is a margin of {col:pnl.margin}. The profit you want at your target margin is {col:pnl.target_profit}. The profit so far this financial year is {col:pnl.cum}.
The result check shows: {col:pnl.state}. The figures come from the Cost Ledger, the Income Ledger, the grants and the asset register and are not audited.
Budget against actual report for a cost code
Budget against actual report of {set:firm}, dated {today}.
The budget for the year is {col:budget.budget}. So far this year {col:budget.actual} was spent, which is {col:budget.used} of the budget.
If costs continue at this pace the year will end at {col:budget.forecast}, which is {col:budget.gap} against the budget. The budget check shows: {col:budget.state}.
The budget holder explains any difference and proposes action before the next monthly close. The budget was last reviewed on {col:budget.reviewed}.
Profit per field report of {set:firm}, dated {today}.
Field: {col:fields.name}. Crop: {col:fields.crop}. Area: {col:fields.area_ha} hectares. Field supervisor: {col:fields.owner}.
This financial year the field earned {col:fields.revenue} and carried costs of {col:fields.cost}, so the profit is {col:fields.profit}.
That is {col:fields.per_ha} per hectare and a margin of {col:fields.margin}. The result check shows: {col:fields.state}.
Only costs charged to this field are counted; farm-wide overheads such as payroll, rent and interest are shown in the monthly profit and loss.

We expect sales of {col:cash.sales_in}, grants of {col:cash.grants_in} and other money in of {col:cash.other_in}, in total {col:cash.inflow}.

We expect running costs of {col:cash.running_out}, machines and works of {col:cash.capex_out}, owner drawings of {col:cash.drawings_out}, loan repayments of {col:cash.loan_out} and tax and licences of {col:cash.tax_out}, in total {col:cash.outflow}.
The net result of the month is {col:cash.net} and the closing cash is {col:cash.closing}, which covers {col:cash.cover_weeks} weeks of costs. The cash check shows: {col:cash.state}.
The amount borrowed was {col:loans.principal} at {col:loans.rate} per year, starting on {col:loans.start} and ending on {col:loans.maturity}. The payment is {col:loans.payment} each month.
So far {col:loans.paid} of the principal has been repaid and the balance is {col:loans.balance}. The next payment is due on {col:loans.next_due}. The loan check shows: {col:loans.state}.
The loan is secured by: {col:loans.collateral}. The interest for the coming year on the balance is about {col:loans.interest_year}.
We applied on {col:grants.applied_on} for {col:grants.applied}. The status is {col:grants.status}. The approved amount is {col:grants.approved} and we received {col:grants.received}.
The amount still to receive is {col:grants.outstanding}. The evidence for the payment claim is due on {col:grants.evidence_due}. The grant check shows: {col:grants.state}.
We keep invoices, photos and the records that the scheme asks for, and we will show them at any inspection.
Event: {col:claims.event} on {col:claims.event_date}, field: {col:claims.field}. We reported it on {col:claims.reported}.
We claim {col:claims.claimed}. The insurer has settled {col:claims.settled}. The status is {col:claims.status} and the claim has been open for {col:claims.days_open} days.
The amount still to receive is {col:claims.outstanding}. The claim check shows: {col:claims.state}. Photos, invoices and the field records are attached to this file.

Open Start and type your farm name, the first day of your financial year, the phone numbers of the manager, the office and the accountant, and your limits: margin you want, minimum cash, warning days and the debt cover your bank wants.
List your cost codes and a budget for each on Budget by Cost Code, with the person who answers for each code.
Enter every bill on Cost Ledger with its cost code and, when it belongs to one, the field, crop or animal group. Type the date you paid.
Enter every sale on Income Ledger with its source, buyer and the field, crop or animal group that earned it. Type the date the money came in.
Add your fields, crops and animal groups on Profit per Field, Profit per Crop and Profit per Animal Group. Revenue, costs and profit fill in.
Add one row for each month on Monthly Profit and Loss and read the profit, the margin and the profit so far this year.
Type the sales, grants and costs you expect on Cash Flow Forecast, and the balances of your accounts on Bank Balances. Loan repayments and tax come in by themselves.
Enter each loan on Loans and Credit Lines and its payments on Repayment Schedule. Type the date you paid each one.
Track grants on Grants and Subsidies, policies on Insurance Policies and claims on Insurance Claims.
List tax and licence payments on Tax and Licence Deadlines, assets on Asset Register, and certificates and permits on Certificates and Permits.
Record audits on Inspections and Audits and the monthly records on Compliance Records. Missing records show in red.
Type each quarter on Key Ratios by Quarter to see the margin, the drawings share, the debt cover and the current ratio against your targets.
Use the 14 calculators for margin, break-even, loans, cash, credit line interest, depreciation, subsidy, insurance claims, working capital, unit cost, assets, debt cover, tax and price rises.
Read Farm Finance Dashboard and Charts every week: profit, budget, cash, loans, grants, insurance, certificates and compliance.
